BiblicalUsage: The word is the act of reading aloud: Paul tells Timothy, 'Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine,' and in the synagogue at Antioch, after the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers sent to Paul and Barnabas asking if they had any word of exhortation. Reading was public, out loud, and it was the centre of the gathering.
TheologicalSignificance: Three verses about public reading carry no doctrine of their own; their weight is the practice — the Scriptures read aloud in the assembly, and then explained.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
